sources: PRE-MARKET RUN: captured Thu Sep 3 2026, ~06:15 UTC / 02:15 ET, before the US cash open and before today's 08:30 ET claims release. Market-priced series are CONFIRMED FRED CLOSES, not vendor headers: T10Y2Y and T5YIFR now carry a SEP 2 print; VIXCLS, BAMLH0A0HYM2, DCOILBRENTEU, SOFR and EFFR are still through SEP 1. Genuinely live overnight prints: Brent, DXY and copper/gold from TradingEconomics as of this timestamp. THEME: THE ESCALATION TRADE GAVE A LITTLE BACK OVERNIGHT. Yesterday's board recorded the first genuine confirmation in five weeks - crude, VIX, MOVE and HY OAS all moving the same way. Overnight that impulse paused rather than extended. Sixth month of the US-Iran conflict. Trump said the latest strikes on Iran 'would be short-lived' while restating that the US controls Hormuz; Tehran retaliated with drones and missiles at US bases across Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq and the UAE. Crucially, oil keeps moving: roughly 8m b/d still transiting the strait, and US Energy Secretary Wright put Monday's flow at 17m barrels, the highest since the war began in late February. CRUDE OFF THE HIGHS: Brent 94.59 live (TradingEconomics, -1.09% on the day) after three straight higher sessions, and after FRED DCOILBRENTEU printed 96.02 for Sep 1. Still +19.2% m/m and +41.2% y/y, and still well above the 88.24 low of Aug 25, but the six-week high has not held. US crude inventories fell 4.5m barrels last week, the first draw since late July. CURVE - NEW PRINT, STILL FLAT: 10Y-2Y 0.40 CONFIRMED Sep 2 (FRED T10Y2Y), unchanged from Sep 1 and against 0.47 on Aug 27. The 7bp of w/w flattening from Friday's hawkish repricing has now held for three sessions rather than reversing. 10Y 4.79 on Sep 1. Still positive, still nowhere near inversion. BREAKEVENS STILL WILL NOT BUDGE - THE KEY NON-CONFIRMATION, NOW WITH A SEP 2 STAMP: T5YIFR 2.33% for SEP 2 (FRED), identical to Sep 1 and inside the 2.31-2.35 band that has held all fortnight. Brent has travelled 88 to 96 and back to 94.6 without moving forward inflation expectations a single basis point. This remains the series that decides whether the supply shock becomes a policy problem, and it is still saying no. EQUITY AND RATES VOL - NO NEW CLOSE: VIX 16.34 confirmed Sep 1 (FRED VIXCLS), up 1.42 points from 14.92 on Aug 31 and the highest close since Aug 20; against 14.51 on Aug 27 the w/w arrow is clearly up. FRED will not carry the Sep 2 close until later today. MOVE 77.88 for Sep 1 (ICE via Investing.com), a third consecutive higher close from 75.32 and roughly 74 a week ago; no Sep 2 print is available from any free source, so the value is carried. Medium confidence on MOVE as always. CREDIT - THE CRACK IS REAL BUT TINY: HY OAS 265bp for Sep 1 (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2), wider for a second straight session from 260 (Aug 28) and 263 (Aug 31). Against 263 on Aug 27 the week-over-week change is +2bp, which is why the arrow reads flat rather than up. Credit has registered the shock and declined to respect it. DOLLAR SOFTER, FUNDING UNCHANGED: DXY 99.388 (TradingEconomics, -0.17% overnight), down from 99.60 yesterday afternoon but above 98.96 on Aug 25, so still up on the week. Six months into a shooting war over the world's most important oil chokepoint there is still no safe-haven dollar bid on the strikes themselves. SOFR 3.66% for Sep 1 against EFFR 3.63%, so SOFR-EFFR is +3bp, up from +1bp a week ago after the 3.68% month-end print on Aug 31 - a normal turn, not stress. SOFR-OIS carried at 3bp. EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis held at -10bp: no free dated quote exists and no funding event in the window justifies a change. COPPER/GOLD LOWER, GOLD BID: copper 6.4963/lb against gold 4,423.73/oz gives 1.469, down from 1.488 yesterday and roughly 1.50 a week ago. Gold is up 0.82% overnight and back above 4,400 - the first session in weeks where the safe-haven asset has actually behaved like one, though the move is small. FREIGHT - NO NEW ASSESSMENT: BDTI 2,699 for Sep 2 (Baltic Exchange via StockQ), +0.86% after the sharp -3.64% drop to 2,676 on Sep 1. Today's assessment publishes around 13:00 London, after this run. Sequence: 3,004 (Aug 21 peak), 2,961, 2,886, 2,851, 2,801, 2,777, [Aug 31 UK bank holiday], 2,676, 2,699. Down 10.2% from the peak and down from 2,801 on Aug 27, so the w/w arrow stays down, but the seven-session slide has stopped. MA5 2,760.80 below MA10 2,857.80. YTD +104.62%. NO NEW PRINTS (carried unchanged): ISM Manufacturing 54.6 for August (released Sep 1), down 1.0 from July's four-year high of 55.6, eighth month of expansion, with prices UNCHANGED at 71.1 - momentum fading while input-cost pressure does not. NFCI -0.558 for the week ending Aug 28 (Chicago Fed), the loosest of the cycle and still easing; next print Wed Sep 9. Initial claims 203k for the week ending Aug 22 (FRED ICSA, down from 207k) - TODAY'S 08:30 ET RELEASE IS THE FIRST LABOUR READ SINCE THE ESCALATION AND LANDS AFTER THIS RUN. Sahm Rule -0.03 for July (FRED SAHMREALTIME), improved from 0.07 in June; August prints tomorrow with payrolls. UMich consumer sentiment 51.7 final for August, down 6.3% from July's 55.2 and the weakest series on the board; FRED UMCSENT still carries only July, so this is taken from the U. Michigan release. LEI 99.5 for July (Conference Board), y/y approximately -1.1%, derived rather than published, negative for four-plus years; next release Sep 18. Building permits 1,433k July SAAR (FRED PERMIT), up from 1,374k. Global liquidity 1=stable: Fed balance sheet 6.731tn on Aug 26 (FRED WALCL), drifting lower for a fortnight but still growing y/y since QT ended Dec 2025; ECB running off, BOJ QT accelerating, PBOC easing. Net neutral. NET READ: yesterday's four-way confirmation did not extend overnight. Brent is 1.2 points off its six-week high, the dollar gave back its bid, and the two series that did print fresh on Sep 2 - the curve at 0.40 and breakevens at 2.33 - both simply repeated Sep 1. The non-confirmation therefore survives intact: forward inflation expectations have not moved through an eight-dollar round trip in crude, HY at 265 is only 2bp wider than a week ago, the NFCI just printed the loosest of the cycle, and funding is clean at 3bp. The domestic soft spots remain the more coherent story: 2s10s 7bp flatter on the week and holding, ISM decelerating with prices stuck at 71.1, freight 10% off its peak, LEI negative y/y, consumer sentiment at 51.7. WATCH: initial claims at 08:30 ET today; payrolls and the August Sahm print tomorrow Fri Sep 4, the single most important number of the week; whether the Sep 2 VIX close confirms or unwinds Tuesday's 1.4-point jump; whether HY OAS widens past 270; and whether Brent holding the mid-90s ever drags T5YIFR out of its 2.31-2.35 band.
